verses.text: These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel across the Jordan, in the wilderness of the Arabah opposite Suf, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It’s an eleven-day walk from Horeb to Kadesh Barnea by way of Mount Seir.
On day one of month eleven in year forty, Moses told the Israelites everything Yahweh had commanded him to tell them.
This was after Moses defeated Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and defeated Og, king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.
Across the Jordan in Moab, Moses began to explain this law:
“Yahweh our God told us at Horeb, ‘You’ve been at this mountain long enough.

Turn around and get moving. Head for the Amorite hill country and all the places around it: the Arabah, the hills, the lowlands, the South, the coast, the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon all the way to the great Euphrates River.
Look, I’ve put the land right in front of you. Go in and take the land Yahweh swore to give your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and their descendants after them.’”
At that time I told you, “I can’t carry all of you by myself.
Yahweh your God has grown your numbers, and now there are as many of you as stars in the sky. ✨
May Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, make you a thousand times more numerous and bless you just as he promised!
How am I supposed to handle all your problems, burdens, and arguments on my own?
Choose wise, understanding, respected men from your tribes, and I’ll put them in charge.”
You answered, “That sounds like the right thing to do.”
So I took wise and respected men from your tribes and put them in charge of you. I appointed commanders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officers for your tribes.
At that time I told your judges, “Hear the cases people bring you and judge fairly between one person and another, including the foreigner living among you.

Don’t play favorites. Listen to the least important person just as you would to the most important. Don’t let anybody intimidate you, because the judgment belongs to God. If a case is too hard for you, bring it to me and I’ll hear it.”
At that time I gave you all the instructions you needed to follow.
We left Horeb and traveled through that huge, frightening wilderness you saw, taking the road to the Amorite hill country as Yahweh our God told us. Then we came to Kadesh Barnea.
I told you, “You’ve reached the Amorite hill country that Yahweh our God is giving us.
Look, Yahweh your God has put the land in front of you. Go up and take it, just as Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, told you. Don’t be afraid or lose heart.”
Every one of you came to me and said, “Let’s send some men ahead to scout the land. They can report back on which road we should take and what towns we’ll come to.”
That seemed like a good idea to me, so I selected twelve men, one from each tribe.
They went up into the hill country, reached the valley of Eshcol, and scouted it.
They brought back some fruit from the land and gave us this report: “The land Yahweh our God is giving us is good.”
But you refused to go up. You went against what Yahweh your God told you to do.
You grumbled in your tents, saying, “Yahweh must hate us. He brought us out of Egypt just to hand us over to the Amorites and have them wipe us out.

Where are we supposed to go? Our brothers have scared us out of our minds. They said, ‘The people are bigger and taller than us. Their cities are huge, with walls that reach the sky. We even saw descendants of the Anakim there!’”
Then I told you, “Don’t panic. Don’t be afraid of them.
Yahweh your God goes ahead of you. He’ll fight for you just as he did in Egypt, right in front of your eyes,
and in the wilderness. You saw how Yahweh your God carried you like a father carries his son, every step of the way until you got here.”
Even after all that, you didn’t trust Yahweh your God.
He went ahead of you on the road to find places for you to put up your tents. He showed you which way to go with fire at night and a cloud by day.
Yahweh heard what you said. He got angry and swore:
“None of the men of this wicked generation will see the good land I promised your ancestors,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He’ll see it. I’ll give the land he walked on to him and his children, because he followed Yahweh wholeheartedly.”
Yahweh was angry with me because of you too. He told me, “You won’t go in either.
Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, will go in. Encourage him, because he’ll lead Israel into its inheritance.
The little ones you said would be captured or killed, your children who don’t yet know good from evil, will go in. I’ll give them the land, and they’ll take possession of it.
As for you, turn around and head into the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea.”
Then you told me, “We’ve sinned against Yahweh. We’ll go up and fight, just as Yahweh our God told us to.” Every one of you strapped on your weapons and figured you could just head up into the hills.
Yahweh told me, “Tell them, ‘Don’t go up or fight. I’m not with you, and your enemies will strike you down.’”
I told you, but you wouldn’t listen. You went against Yahweh’s command and marched up into the hills anyway.
The Amorites who lived in those hills came out against you. They chased you like bees and beat you back through Seir as far as Hormah.
You came back and cried before Yahweh, but he wouldn’t listen to you or turn his ear toward you.
So you stayed in Kadesh for a long time, all those days you spent there.
